nodes.summary: NONOGRAM is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of nonogram instances, to a feasible nonogram instance. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The NONOGRAM decision problem

nodes.summary: A nonogram instance with row clues $R_0, \dots, R_{m-1}$ and column clues $C_0, \dots, C_{n-1}$ is feasible when there is a picture, a list of $m$ rows of Booleans each of length $n$, such that for every $r < m$ the run list of row $r$ equals $R_r$, and for every $c < n$ the run list of column $c$, read from row $0$ to row $m - 1$, equals $C_c$.
nodes.title: Feasible nonogram instances

nodes.summary: A nonogram instance is a pair $(R, C)$ of finite lists, the row clues $R$ and the column clues $C$, where each clue is a finite list of natural numbers.
nodes.title: Nonogram instances

nodes.summary: The NONOGRAM decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to NONOGRAM by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: NONOGRAM is NP-complete

nodes.summary: For a Boolean $b$ and a pair $(k, R)$ of a natural number $k$ and a finite list $R$ of natural numbers, the step returns $(k + 1, R)$ if $b$ is true. If $b$ is false it returns $(0, R)$ when $k = 0$, and $(0, R')$ when $k > 0$, where $R'$ is the list $R$ with $k$ prepended.
nodes.title: One step of the run-length computation

nodes.summary: For a finite list $l$ of Booleans, the runs of $l$ are its maximal blocks of consecutive true entries. The run list of $l$ is the list of the lengths of these blocks, in order from left to right; it is empty when $l$ has no true entry.
nodes.title: Run lengths of a row

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
